title: Why Your Hand Reaches For Biscuits Before Your Brain Decides
hook: Ever grabbed a biscuit and thought, wait, why did I do that?

narration.text: Your hand can reach for a biscuit before you consciously decide to eat one.
That is because habits do not live in your thinking brain at all.
Repeated actions get stored as automatic routines in a deeper part of the brain.
A cue, like the biscuit tin, triggers the routine before thought even kicks in.
That is called automaticity, and it saves mental effort for everything else you do.
The catch is it does not know you are dieting, it just knows the cue.
Willpower rarely beats this, because the habit fires before willpower gets a say.
Changing the cue, like moving the tin, works better than fighting the urge.
Notice the moment your hand moves before your mind catches up, what triggers yours?

description: Ever wonder why your hand grabs a biscuit before you have even decided to eat one? This short explains automaticity, the brain process behind habits, and why changing your environment beats relying on willpower.
topic: Why your hand might involuntarily reach for a biscuit even when you are on a diet, explaining automaticity in habit formation.
